Situation1: They travel a long distance to participate in an important religious festival, ensuring they fully engage in all rituals and offerings.
Expectation2: Raise public awareness about social inequities and marginalized groups
Situation2: They respond to an urgent incident of discrimination that requires immediate public attention and awareness.
Story: I had been looking forward to the festival for weeks, the anticipation building as I traveled the long distance to my family’s village. The air was thick with the scent of incense and marigolds, and my relatives greeted me with warmth, expecting me to join every ritual and offering. As a Hindu, it was my duty to honor the gods and traditions, to be present and engaged in every ceremony. But just as the main puja was about to begin, my phone buzzed with an urgent message—a case of blatant discrimination against a marginalized group had erupted in the city. As an advocate, I was expected to respond immediately, to raise public awareness and stand up for justice. My mind raced, torn between the sacred rituals unfolding before me and the desperate voices calling for help. The weight of both worlds pressed down on me, each demanding my full presence, each unwilling to wait. My heart pounded as I stood at the threshold, caught between devotion and duty, unable to silence the clamor of either role.
